Basic notions of Waves and Electromagnetism
Basic notions of Fundamentals of Computer Science

learning_outcomes.text: Provide the student with basic knowledge about the utility of automatic control systems and their applications in industry and consumer products.
Enable the student to mathematically describe and analyze the behavior of a system in the time and frequency domain, using simulation tools.
Enable the student to tune controllers in simple control structures.
Know and identify the elements involved in instrumentation for industrial process control and automation and their functions.
Configure and program simple applications in industrial control devices.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to process automation and control.
Automation: Introduction to automation. Elements of automation. Regulations. Grafcet diagrams. Programming using SFC and ST.
System modeling: Systems and signals. Functional diagrams. Transfer function. Block diagrams. State-space modeling. System linearization.
System analysis: Stability. Overdamped and underdamped natural modes. Time response.

System control: Introduction to control. Steady-state analysis in feedback systems. Transient analysis of feedback systems. Root locus. PID design in the time domain. Digital implementation of regulators.
Frequency domain: Concept of frequency response. Bode and polar diagrams. Time-frequency relationships. Frequency analysis of feedback systems. Regulator design in frequency.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary examination, a minimum score of 4 out of 10 is required for the theoretical block. If this minimum is met, the theoretical grade is calculated as (0.25 × T1) + (0.75 × T2), and the final grade is (0.2 × T1) + (0.6 × T2) + (0.2 × P). Otherwise, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. For the extraordinary examination, a theoretical exam (TEX) and a practical exam (P) are conducted, with the practical grade from the ordinary call being maintained if passed. A minimum of 4 out of 10 is required in the theoretical part (TEX), and the final grade is calculated as (0.8 × TEX) + (0.2 × P); otherwise, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0.
